reflections.summary: Lost 0-2 in a series decided by team-building mismatches rather than pilot errors (zero decision errors across both games). In Game 2, the core problem was inability to break through the opponent's Regenerator Slowbro + Sitrus Berry recovery loop protected by frequent Protect usage. Excadrill (Mold Breaker Earthquake) was the only source of meaningful damage but was burned and chipped to death by Slowbro after eliminating Arcanine and Empoleon. Rotom-Wash was Choice-locked into Thunderbolt and could not pivot, leaving it trapped into unfavorable matchups. Charizard-Mega-Y burned its entire Drought turn charging Solar Beam then immediately died to Arcanine and Slowbro's super-effective hits — wasting the Mega slot and sun. Weavile burned its Focus Sash surviving Arcanine's Flare Blitz critical hit, then got revenge-killed next turn. The team lacked sustained special offense to wear down bulky Regenerator recovery and had no dedicated Toxic user. Toxapex, left behind, would have provided crucial bulk, Toxic for Slowbro, and reliable recovery. The opponent's balanced core of Slowbro/Arcanine/Gengar/Empoleon punished the glass-heavy four brought.
reflections.adjustment: 1) Swap Venusaur (redundant with Charizard-Y for sun, both weather-dependent) for Toxapex — provides Toxic to break Regenerator Slowbro, reliable recovery, and a physical wall against Arcanine's Intimidate users. 2) Give Rotom-Wash a Choice Specs set with Volt Switch access (or use Assault Vest) to maintain pivoting flexibility instead of being locked into Thunderbolt. 3) Reconsider Charizard-Y Mega timing — lead with Fire Blast pressure instead of charging Solar Beam into double super-effective hits. 4) Consider bringing a dedicated breaker (e.g., Absol or Scizor from the bench) that can threaten Arcanine and outspeed/OHKO Gengar before NastyPlot. 5) Preserve Excadrill for late-game cleaning; do not burn its Mold Breaker Earthquake early against Arcanine into Protect.
reflections.notebook: DURABLE OPPONENT TENDENCIES: Slowbro runs Regenerator + Sitrus Berry, heals 33% per switch and more with Slack Off; must be worn by Toxic or repeated super-effective hits. Arcanine uses Intimidate on first physical contact plus Shuca Berry to neuter Earthquake/Earth Power; Intimidate stacks if it switches back in. Protect is spammed defensively — respect it, never double into it. Gengar NastyPlot sets up on passive switches; revenge-kill priority needed (Weavile Ice Shard or similar). Empoleon Leftovers tank takes two super-effective hits easily; Flash Cannon + Ice Beam coverage is wide. Grimmsnarl (Prankster Light Screen/Reflect) and Lucario (Expert Belt Close Combat) are unused but prepare for them as potential surprise leads or late-game cleaners. STRATEGIC FACTS REVEALED: Slowbro Calm nature, Sitrus Berry consumed by turn 8, Regenerator confirmed. Arcanine Impish nature, Intimidate confirmed, Shuca Berry consumed turn 7. Gengar Timid, Cursed Body, NastyPlot + ShadowBall + Thunderbolt + DazzlingGleam. Empoleon Calm, Torrent, Leftovers, ChillingWater + FlashCannon + IceBeam + Protect. Choice-locked Rotom-Wash cannot pivot — opponent will exploit this. PREP CONCLUSIONS: Toxapex should replace one redundant sun member; provides Toxic and bulk against this archetype. Need at least one faster revenge killer with priority or strong neutral hit to stop Gengar NastyPlot sweeps. Earthquake Mold Breaker is the best tool against this team — keep Excadrill healthy for late game. Sun team alone is insufficient; opponent's recovery core outlasts weather-dependent offense.

reflections.summary: Won game 2 and series 2-0 because leading Slowbro+Arcanine (not Gengar) quickly removed Mega Charizard Y under sun and then Weavile, while Slowbro's Protect/Scald burn and Arcanine Intimidate wore down Excadrill; final Slowbro survived Earthquake at 31%. Between-game adjustment of not leading Mega Gengar (kept unmegaed) avoided early Rotom disruption and helped. Team-preview brought Gengar, Empoleon, Slowbro, Arcanine: Slowbro/Arcanine suited opponent perfectly; Empoleon was dead weight (died to Rotom/Excadrill) and Gengar underused. Series prep: registered six (Mega Gengar, Grimmsnarl, Arcanine, Empoleon, Slowbro, Lucario) mostly fit—Slowbro/Arcanine correct, but lack of Ground move for Rotom was a gap; left-behind Garchomp would have given needed Ground coverage.
reflections.adjustment: For a future rematch, register Garchomp (left behind) instead of Empoleon to supply Ground moves vs Rotom-Wash and Excadrill, and only Mega Evolve Gengar after Rotom is removed. Keep Slowbro+Arcanine lead. Consider Grimmsnarl for screens if needed, but current core works.
reflections.notebook: Opponent series team: Charizard-Mega-Y (Modest sun), Weavile (Jolly Pressure), Excadrill (Adamant Mold Breaker LO), Rotom-Wash (Timid Choice Scarf, locks Thunderbolt), plus unbred Toxapex (Bold Regen), Venusaur (Modest Chlorophyll). Tendencies: aggressive lead with sun + priority Weavile, mid-game Rotom switch for Electric lock, Excadrill late cleaner. Strategic facts: Rotom choice-locked after entry; Excadrill weak to Fire/Water/Fight/Ground; no Fighting/Ground on their seen moves. Prep conclusions: Slowbro+Arcanine lead beats their lead; avoid leading Gengar vs Rotom; need Ground coverage (Garchomp) for Rotom; Empoleon unnecessary; Mega Gengar best post-Rotom.
